result.title: AGL-SKILL: Coding Harnesses as Agentic Optimizers
result.summary: Frontier models are increasingly used through harnesses as agents, with growing autonomy to do useful work. Agent performance can often be enhanced by the use of skills: reusable workflows, code, and prompts that provide task-related information or guide the behaviour of the model. Skills, being textual in nature, present themselves as another editable surface to be optimized; current methods have improved on handcrafting and one-shot generation by treating skill development as an iterative process, using score-driven search to tweak and improve performance. In this paper, we demonstrate the efficacy of the agents themselves as optimizers: across five benchmarks, a coding agent without guidance substantially improves every target and outperforms published skill-optimization methods. More broadly, this shows the capability of agents to do such work and to refine their own behaviour to provide task-specific context, as long as they are given a metric to measure against.

AI.brief_summary: 论文将 skill（可复用的工作流、代码与提示）视为可编辑的优化对象，用 coding agent 自身在给定评价指标下迭代改写 skill，并在五个基准上超过已发表的 skill 优化方法。
AI.relevance_reason: 其“以指标为信号、由 agent 自行搜索并改写行为上下文”的闭环，或可启发 LVR 中对推理脚手架与 latent 推理策略的自动调优及监督分配，但作用面是文本 skill 而非内部状态，需核查能否迁移。
